item.title: Ruben Amorim delivers honest Scudetto verdict after Milan conquer Inter in Derby della Madonnina
item.description: AC Milan v Bologna FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Ruben Amorim has admitted that while winning the Scudetto remains a concrete goal for AC Milan, the club must remain realistic about the timeframe required for such a project. The Portuguese tactician guided the Rossoneri to a vital victory over rivals Inter, marking their fourth consecutive win in Serie A. Addressing the Scudetto ambitions Amorim could not hide his satisfaction after witnessing his Milan side dismantle Inter in a high-stakes Derby della Madonnina. Despite the euphoria of a derby win, Amorim was quick to temper expectations regarding an immediate title charge. While owner Gerry Cardinale has set clear objectives for the management, the Portuguese coach believes that building a championship-winning side is a gradual process that cannot be rushed. He urged the fans and the media to be honest about the journey the club is currently undertaking in its new era. "Cardinale gave us a goal, but the important thing is to win these games. Things won't change in a month, two months, or a year. It takes time, but also magical nights like this. This victory won't change our situation. The Scudetto? It's possible, but I don't know when. We have to be honest . People aren't stupid, but they understand and see that this team is improving," Amorim told Sky Sport Italia . Tactical discipline key to derby triumph The Rossoneri manager praised the mental fortitude shown by his squad, particularly given the tight turnaround following their midweek fixture. Amorim highlighted the focus displayed by his players from the opening whistle, suggesting he felt a positive result was brewing early in the contest. "It's especially important after Wednesday's game. We wanted to celebrate even more. I'm proud of what the lads achieved with so little rest after Bologna. I'm happy and proud," he said. "I always try to interpret what the team tells me, but right from the start I had the feeling we were competitive; the team was focused and calm, and that's why I always had confidence." Player performance and defensive solidity While stars like Christian Pulisic, Luka Modric, and Adrien Rabiot grabbed the headlines for their creative output, Amorim was eager to share the credit with his entire squad. He specifically praised the defensive contributions of those who have stepped up recently, emphasizing that the collective effort is what makes the team competitive. The ability to rotate players like Matteo Gila while maintaining a cohesive structure was a major takeaway for the coaching staff. "It's not just those three players, but I like the concentration of the whole team, like Pavlovic and De Winter and the way they took the field, then there are Rabiot, Pulisic and Moreira but we were all very good," he stated. item.title: Makai Lemon's emergence could change Eagles' receiver rotation
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles have struggled to produce consistently on offense during their five-game losing streak, but rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon is showing encouraging development at a position hit hard by injuries. Lemon delivered one of the most important offensive plays of Monday night's 38-21 loss to Dallas, catching his first career touchdown pass from Tanner McKee during the third quarter to give Philadelphia a brief 21-20 lead. The score capped a productive possession that included a fourth-and-1 play-action completion to Lemon, highlighting the growing trust between the rookie receiver and Philadelphia's starting quarterback. For first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, Lemon's emergence creates another opportunity to expand the passing game while evaluating the receiving rotation as injured veterans return. Philadelphia has dealt with injuries to DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (both ruled out), forcing different receivers into expanded roles and limiting the offense's ability to establish consistent chemistry. Lemon has responded by demonstrating the route-running ability and versatility that made him one of the most intriguing receivers in the 2026 draft. His production against Dallas showed the Eagles can create opportunities for him beyond occasional designed touches. The bigger question is how Philadelphia distributes its passing-game opportunities once Smith and Wicks are healthy. The Eagles also have Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore, and Darius Cooper in the receiving group, giving Mannion several options when constructing different personnel packages. However, Philadelphia cannot afford to overlook a rookie who has shown the ability to create separation and contribute in high-leverage situations. With McKee replacing Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season, developing reliable connections with younger receivers has become especially important. The Eagles rank near the bottom of the NFL in scoring and total offense, making explosive plays and successful third-down conversions increasingly valuable. Lemon's touchdown against Dallas provided one of the few encouraging moments during another disappointing defeat. Philadelphia should not expect one rookie receiver to correct every problem facing its offense, but expanding Lemon's responsibilities could help establish a more productive passing attack. The Eagles will have another opportunity to evaluate his development Sunday night against Washington, a defense that has struggled to prevent opponents from finishing drives with touchdowns. If Lemon continues producing when given opportunities, Philadelphia's coaching staff will struggle to reduce his role simply because other receivers return. The rookie has earned a chance to become a regular contributor, and his development could have implications extending well beyond the team's disappointing 2026 start. item.title: College Football fans are missing their villains
item.description: Jan 7, 2010; Pasadena, CA, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Nick Saban holds up the Coaches' Trophy and celebrates after defeating the Texas Longhorns 37-21 in the 2010 BCS national championship game at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Over the past couple of weeks, I’ve seen quite a few college football personalities lamenting the current state of college football, as the passion just doesn’t seem up to par for the sport. There does seem to be a bit of fan malaise, and the finger is often pointed at unfettered free agency. That is the root cause of the issue, as backups leaving rather than sticking around to start as upperclassmen has weakened the depth of top tier programs and improved the starting squads of the middle tier. As a result the sport no longer has a true villain to hate, and petty hate watching is the backbone of college football fanaticism. For the better part of two decades, Nick Saban was the sport’s lightning rod, his Crimson Tide the designated villain. With life changing money not yet a part of the equation for student athletes, Saban was able to sell his development program to stack the two deep with NFL talent. Alabama routinely redshirted players that could have started immediately at 50 programs across the country, and that depth resulted in a dynasty that every other fanbase united against. Even fanbases that hated one another could bond over watching the dynasty fall. “We Want Bama” became a meme. Alabama fans dominated the TV ratings as more people watched hoping to see them lose than to see them win. Alabama certainly isn’t the only program that could call itself a villain over the past couple of decades. Big Ten fanbases have had a similar dynamic with Ohio State, Big 12 fanbases despised Texas before they left, and hating Notre Dame is something that many fanbases can rally behind. Saban simply won more than anyone else for a long time and managed to unite fanbases across the country. This isn’t unique to college football. Fans that are nostalgic for “golden ages” of various sports remember the NBA dominated by the Lakers and Celtics, then Jordan’s Bulls. The Yankees were the team to hate in Major League Baseball, and thanks to the economics of the sport Los Angeles has now taken that mantle. At various times the Steelers, 49ers, Cowboys, and Patriots have been the villains of the NFL. Like Saban’s hey day at Alabama, millions of fans would watch those teams hoping to see them taste defeat. Winning a disproportionate amount is the primary driver of that villain arc and, thanks to parity driven by NIL and the portal, right now nobody in college football is consistently dominating. There simply isn’t anyone to drive the same level of hate that sustains interest in college football. Playoff expansion hasn’t helped matters. item.title: Tributes paid to 'inspirational' Ciara Mageean after death at 34
item.description: A statement posted on her social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved ones [Getty Images] Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34. Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025. She represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024. The athlete also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022. A statement posted on her social media on Sunday said she had died at 06:30 GMT on Sunday, surrounded by her loved ones. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said. Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to long-term partner Thomas Moran. 'One of our own' Down GAA said it was "honoured and privileged" to call Mageean one of its own, describing her as someone who never forgot her roots. It said she had remained closely connected to her local GAA community, attending matches and supporting clubs. Mageean won a gold medal at the 2024 European Championships in Rome [Getty Images] "She touched the lives of so many people and she helped change the lives of so many," it said. "In her battle with illness she showed us courage, positivity and the value of life." Her former school, Assumption Grammar School, said it was "deeply saddened and heartbroken" by the death of its "cherished past pupil". "Ciara's kindness, strength, faith and unwavering determination were an inspiration to us all," it said. "She touched countless lives with her warmth, humility and generosity of spirit." 'A champion in every sense of the word' Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill described Mageean as "a champion in every sense of the word and a role model for all athletes". "She represented her country with pride and helped put Irish athletics on the map," she said in a statement. O'Neill said Mageean had faced her cancer diagnosis with the same "bravery and determination" she had shown throughout her sporting career. "Ciara's legacy will live on and she will continue to be an inspiration to many." Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly said people across Northern Ireland had been "deeply proud and inspired" by the athlete. Writing on social media, she described Mageean as an "outstanding athlete and ambassador for her sport" who had spoken with honesty and bravery about her health battles. Communities Minister Gordon Lyons said he was "deeply saddened" by Mageean's death and said she was an "inspiration to so many". Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin said he was "deeply saddened" by her untimely death and extended his sympathies to her husband Thomas, family and friends. item.title: Barcelona identify 23-year-old star as leading candidate for January sale to fund defensive signing
item.description: Barcelona identify 23-year-old star as leading candidate for January sale to fund defensive signing Barcelona are preparing to strengthen their defence in January, with the club currently struggling with the number of players out injured. The back line was already the Catalan club’s weakest area, and Barça ‘s decision not to strengthen it in the summer has come back to haunt them. Now, the club look keen to address this in January, but their financial situation could force them into a difficult decision. Hansi Flick wants to add another centre-back to his squad, and Barcelona will, in all likelihood, have to make a sale to fund the signing. According to MARCA , Alejandro Balde has emerged as the leading candidate to leave the club in January. The 23-year-old has struggled to convince Hansi Flick this season and has not started a single game under the German manager. Barcelona need a sale before making a January signing Flick and sporting director Deco are interested in adding another central defender following the start of the season. However, the club only want to sign someone capable of genuinely improving the team and do not want to add a player for the sake of it. “We are always looking for what is best for the team. If we can do something, perhaps we will,” Flick explained recently. Balde is unable to get a minute at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The financial obstacle remains substantial. Barcelona may need to make financial room before pursuing a marquee player. Selling someone like Balde for a decent fee could allow the Catalan club to put the money to good use in a couple of months’ time. Balde’s Barcelona career seems over Balde has gone from an undisputed starter at Barcelona to a player who is simply unable to get a start. Against Deportivo Alaves last night, Hansi Flick chose to put Brian Farinas in the XI ahead of him and only gave Balde around 30 minutes in the second half. With Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart established at left-back, it is highly unlikely that Balde will get minutes once everyone is fit. Hansi Flick has repeatedly insisted that he is not happy with what the Spaniard is showing in training and that he lacks the confidence to play in his system. Where does Alejandro Balde go from here? (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) However, Balde remains reluctant to leave Barcelona. He rejected the possibility during the summer and continues to believe he can regain Flick’s confidence. For the club, selling an academy graduate would be a major call. Once touted for stardom, Balde’s career seems to be going nowhere. The challenge is ensuring Barcelona do not make a rash decision on Balde, considering he is just 23 and has his entire career ahead of him. However, if a sacrifice has to be made in January, Balde looks like the most likely name on the chopping block, and it remains to be seen how the Spaniard’s future pans out.

item.description: The Buffalo Bills are hoping to have tight end Dalton Kincaid in the lineup when they take on the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8 on Sunday afternoon. The Bills came out of their bye and Kincaid emerged at less than 100%, as evidenced by the team putting him on the injury report with a chest injury. Kincaid made it through the week with three limited practices before he was slapped with the questionable tag on Friday. Now, here’s what we know about his chances of suiting up in the Week 8 game versus the Ravens. Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) We don’t have a concrete answer on Kincaid’s status for Week 8 just yet, but we do have a good indication he will go. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported on Saturday that Kincaid is “pretty confident” that he’s going to suit up against Baltimore, and it’s not hard to see why after he logged three limited practices during the week. Of course, we’re still going to confirm Kincaid is active when the Bills drop their inactives an hour and a half before their 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) We’re old enough to remember when Kincaid looked like he was going to have a phenomenal 2026 season after he ripped off 12 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown over his first two games. However, Kincaid hasn’t come close to matching that production over his last four games combined, with the Bills tight end reeling in 11 catches for 90 scoreless yards in that span. This matchup with the Ravens is a middle-of-the-road one, with the Ravens giving up the 17th-fewest fantasy points per game to tight ends, per CBS Sports . There is absolutely justification for sitting Kincaid, but given the matchup, the shallow pool of tight ends and Kincaid’s potential for elite production any given week, he can once again be started if you don’t have a more consistent tight end on your roster. item.title: NBA fans have a lot to say after Jaylen Brown’s heated exchange with Grayson Allen
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Jaylen Brown and Grayson Allen got into a heated exchange during the Philadelphia 76ers’ game on the road against the Charlotte Hornets. Brown scored 16 points, while also contributing 4 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals on the night. While he did not have the best scoring night, Tyrese Maxey came up big with a 38-point performance to lead the 76ers to a 109-104 win. This was the 76ers’ sixth win of the season against a Hornets team who have played some good basketball this season. Even in this game, the Hornets held an 83-77 lead going into the fourth quarter, but the 76ers once again showed some late-game resurgence and went on a 13-0 run to take the win. As the game was getting intense in the fourth quarter, Brown and Grayson Allen both scrambled to the floor for a loose ball. As Allen was trying to get up, Brown pushed Allen away, leading to a heated exchange between the two. Their teammates came running in to separate the two players, but the situation was quickly resolved with the referee assessing technicals to both Brown and Allen. Fans amazed as commentator calls Jaylen Brown as Jaylen Tatum While it was a heated moment on the court, fans who were listening to the commentary got a great laugh out of the incident as the commentator named Jaylen Brown as Jaylen Tatum. Brown and Tatum, who were teammates with the Boston Celtics, have been in a public back-and-forth, with both players expressing their feelings about each other. Tatum maintained his stance that he wasn’t aware of Brown’s departure, but the 2024 Finals MVP was not having it. Below a viral video of Tatum; Brown replied with a cap emoji, indicating that his former teammate was lying. Many have chimed in with their thoughts on the rivalry, but the commentator’s mistake seemed to attract a funny reaction among fans. One fan said: “Announcer is a m* troll LMAO “Jaylen Tatum.” While another added: “Bro called him Jaylen Tatum,” with several laughing face emojis. Someone also posed a question: “Jalen Tatum ???????? who’s Jalen Tatum ????” There were a few who were not pleased with what Allen did during the play. “Can’t stand him since his Duke days…he just does too much too often,” wrote one fan. item.title: Bears vs. Seahawks Preview: Chicago needs to locate Nick Emmanwori
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 4: Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks in action during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Lumen Field on October 4, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll is joined by former Chicago Bears cornerback Jerry Azumah to talk about the newest Chicago Bears player, Jeffery Simmons, and the immediate impact he’ll have on this defense. They also dive into the Bears v. Seattle Seahawks game and what it will take for the Bears to upset the defending champion on the road. Taylor is then joined by Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times, who shares the Seahawks’ perspective after they made a big trade for Quenton Nelson to try to spark their run game and protect Sam Darnold. Taylor and Bob chat about all things Seattle, plus this possible chess match between Ben Johnson and Mike Macdonald, and how Macdonald’s defense will attack the Bears. “They don’t blitz a ton. You know, traditionally, they’re not the biggest blitzing team ever. What they do more is try to bring pressure from different spots than you’ll see,” Condotta said. “So, it’s not always necessarily bringing like six guys, but it’s bringing four or five guys, but not from spots you necessarily thought those guys were coming from.” Condotta then discussed Seattle’s biggest X factor. “And that’s where Nick Emmanwori has become such a factor because he’s basically, essentially a strong side linebacker, but people make a big deal out of the Seahawks always playing nickel because they look at Emmanwori being listed as a safety, but you know, essentially a strong side linebacker. But you know, they can put him on the defensive line, and he’s just like a rush end.” ”It makes it kind of hard to know what they’re doing with him on this play, where what is he going to do, and you know you can rush him and drop someone else, and that’s where I think McDonald is really at his most dangerous is devising things like that.“ Besides previewing the game, Azumah also got into the big Simmons trade, and what else he’d like to see the Bears do. “I would like to see a defensive back, particularly a corner, to go over to the Chicago Bears,” he said about another possible trade. “I think that they could use the depth. There’ve been some issues in the secondary, but you know, Dennis Allen, he runs a very precise system, and the DBs have to basically match up to the wide receivers, and sometimes they lose. So I think that with Simmons being there, I think that that’s going to help out the secondary tremendously, but I wouldn’t mind seeing a depth move at corner.” Check out the full show in either of the embeds below, or anywhere you get your podcasts. item.title: UFC Halloween, The Morning After: Did Jacobe Smith Live Up To The Hype?
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 31: Jacobe Smith reacts after a victory against Randy Brown of Jamaica in a welterweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on October 31, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) If Saturday’s UFC Halloween event was supposed to be Jacobe Smith’s “big moment” then the undefeated prospect left a lot of people wanting more. Smith, who came into Saturday’s co-main event a sizeable betting favorite, was pitted against welterweight veteran Randy Brown. “Rude Boy” has been around for a while now and he’s fought a lot of different styles so fans were intrigued to see how Smith would handle the step up in competition. After all, Smith has dominated his opponents to date, but Brown was the first welterweight name that carried some real weight. If Smith couldn’t get past Brown with flying colors then maybe he’s not the “top prospect” we all thought. On paper, Smith didn’t disappoint. He showed off his usual athleticism while staying aggressive and in full control of the fight. He even split Brown open after launching a barrage of slicing elbows from top position. Brown didn’t do much damage from his end, but he did survive all three rounds. It was a pretty lopsided win in favor of Smith, who is now 5-0 as a member of the UFC’s welterweight division. That’s all well and good, but fans wanted more from Smith. The 30-year-old knockout artist has looked unstoppable over his first four Octagon appearances, which included four total finishes and some of the biggest takedown slams you’ll ever see. Smith has even been talking smack to UFC veteran Kevin Holland to create some extra buzz. Not to mention the athletic gifts and incredible finishing ability that Smith possesses. Because of all that, seeing Smith get his hand raised with a decision win was a bit disappointing. Brown was there for the taking, but Smith finally met an opponent he couldn’t finish. UFC matchmakers will likely push Smith even further his next time out so he will have a shot at redemption to truly cement his name as the next best thing. item.title: Miyu Yamashita wins third title of 2026, successfully defends Maybank
item.description: Miyu Yamashita set a record as the fastest Japanese player to reach five wins on the LPGA, needing only 46 starts. The 4-foot-11 star joins the top 2 players in the world – Nelly Korda and Jeeno Thitikul – as the only players on tour this season with three or more wins. Yamashita, who came into the week No. 4 in the world, picked up her third title this season with a two-stroke victory at the Maybank Championship in steamy Malaysia. She finished at 22 under for the tournament, successfully defending her title at Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club. Last year, Yamashita won the event in a sudden-death playoff. She bested her 72-hole scoring mark by four strokes this year. More: 2026 Maybank Championship prize money payouts for each LPGA player in Malaysia "I didn't expect and think I am going to win today," said 25-year-old Yamashita, who has yet to lose on the LPGA when holding the 54-hole lead. A total of three players have successfully defended titles this season: Hyo Joo Kim (Ford Championship presented by Wildhorse Pass) and Jeeno Thitikul (Mizuho Americas Open) and Yamashita (Maybank). Yamashita's mark of five wins in 46 starts as a member bests the record set by Ayako Okamoto, who needed 71 official starts to reach five wins between 1981 and 1984. Yamashita also won the Aramco Korea Championship on the LET earlier this month. In her last seven starts worldwide, Yamashita has four wins and three additional top-8 finishes. China's Yan Liu gave Yamashita a good run on Sunday, carding 33 on the front nine, highlighted by an eagle at the par-5 fifth. The runner-up mark's Liu's career-best finish on the LPGA and her lowest 72-hole score. View this post on Instagram Frenchwoman Pauline Roussin-Bouchard tied for third with amateur Marisa Tojai of Thailand. At 17, Tojai was the youngest player in the field. Roussin-Bouchard's finish moved her up from No. 79 to No. 58 in the Race to the CME Globe, putting her in prime position to qualify for the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship (top 60). Mirabel Ting was the leading Malaysian player in the field. The former Florida State star finished at 5 under for the event in a share of 48th. Ting was the Player of the Year on the Epson Tour this season, earning her LPGA card for the 2027 season. She played this week on a sponsor invitation. item.title: How Constant Losing Could Impact Kings’ Darius Acuff Jr.’s Development
item.description: Sacramento Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. (5) handles the ball against Memphis Grizzlies guard Jahmai Mashack (21) during the fourth quarter at FedExForum. Photo Credit: Petre Thomas, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor A player’s development should not focus solely on personal statistics and achievements; it involves more than that. One such young NBA player to whom this applies is Darius Acuff Jr. of the Sacramento Kings. Early in his career, he faces a tough challenge as he tries to develop while playing for a team that struggles to win. Even though Acuff makes a strong impression with his offensive skills, one may wonder what impact the losing will have on his development. Individual Success in a Losing Environment It is easy to see why the Kings have such high hopes for Acuff just by looking at his individual numbers. Averaging 24 points and 6.6 assists in the first five games, Acuff dropped a career-high 38 points against the Memphis Grizzlies on Halloween. It was his second straight 30-point game and third in his last five outings. Unfortunately, despite his recent strong performance, Sacramento lost, dropping to 0-6. So, the player showed he can create offense and take on a lot of responsibility, but it is also clear that it’s hard to show your skills and still lose. The most dangerous thing about losing all the time in basketball is the psychological toll it can take. This sport requires a lot of confidence, and confidence comes from victories. Constantly being defeated, Acuff may feel pressure to score more points and play more aggressively because his individual success doesn’t give the Kings a chance to win. Sacramento Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. (5) reacts during the third quarter against the Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum. Photo Credit: Petre Thomas, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Challenges and Opportunities of Adversity The adverse conditions of losing can also affect Acuff’s leadership development. As a point guard, Acuff is expected to organize the attack, communicate, and make decisions that help the whole group. But this constant deficit can make the point guard’s tasks harder and lead to individual problem-solving. Nevertheless, early experience overcoming adversity can also help develop patience, accountability, and the ability to keep other players motivated regardless of the results. Another problem is that it can be harder to evaluate a rookie’s development. It usually takes time for a rookie to adjust to the NBA pace, become more efficient on defense, develop shot selection, and understand when to score or assist others. Scoring numbers show Acuff’s high level of offensive responsibility , but the Kings’ staff should also consider his efficiency and playmaking. Another risk of losing too much is forming habits that are difficult to break. item.title: World Wrestling Championships: U.S. wins most gold medals outright for first time in history
item.description: Spencer Lee and Levi Haines claimed titles on the last day of the World Wrestling Championships, ensuring the U.S. won the most gold medals outright at a full worlds for the first time. Lee (57kg) and Haines (79kg) pushed the Americans to seven total titles at worlds in Kazakhstan, one more than Iran. Seven matched the most titles that the U.S. has ever won at a single worlds (2022). The U.S. matched its program record for total medals with 15. The U.S. also won the most golds at the 2012 Worlds with two, an edition with women's events only. The other Americans to win earlier in the meet were Adaugo Nwachukwu (62kg) and Everest Leydecker (55kg) in women's freestyle and Bo Bassett (65kg), Kyle Dake (86kg) and Kyle Snyder (97kg) in men's freestyle. Lee, the 2024 Olympic silver medalist who missed the podium at 2025 Worlds, beat Roman Bravo-Young of Mexico 10-0 in Sunday's 57kg final. Match video is here . Lee came back from tearing an ACL (for a fourth time) about three months ago. "I was going to concede the spot (on the U.S. team)," said a tearful Lee , sporting a black eye. "I go, you know, I've done it before, and I said I'll just go win it anyways. "I don't got many more tears left in me, so I don't know if I'll be back next year. I'll probably have to have surgery." In Saturday's semifinals, Lee pinned Islam Bazarganov of Azerbaijan while down 10-5. Haines, an NCAA champion for Penn State this past March, followed his silver at 79kg in 2025 with gold on Sunday. He beat Mohammad Nokhodi of Iran 4-3 in the final of the non-Olympic weight class, one year after losing his final by one point. Match video is here . At 92kg, another non-Olympic weight, American Trent Hidlay followed his 2025 gold with silver. Russian Amanula Gadzhimagomedov beat Hidlay 3-2. item.title: Todd McLellan Sends Blunt Warning After Red Wings’ Stunning Collapse
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings appeared to be cruising toward their third consecutive victory Saturday afternoon. Instead, they delivered one of their most frustrating losses of the young season. Detroit squandered a two-goal third-period lead in a stunning 5-4 loss to the St. Louis Blues at Little Caesars Arena, surrendering three unanswered goals in just 4:38. And afterward, head coach Todd McLellan made it clear that what happened was unacceptable. His biggest concern wasn’t the final score. It was how quickly his team abandoned the habits that had put it in position to win. Oct 24, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Detroit Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan on his bench against the Calgary Flames during the first period at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Todd McLellan Calls Out Red Wings Following Collapse McLellan didn’t blame bad luck or an unfortunate bounce for Detroit’s defeat. Instead, he pointed directly to his team’s execution and attention to detail. “We got sloppy,” McLellan said following Saturday’s loss . “You’ve heard me use the word checking. Those checking skills, I think the intent was still there but the execution and the details in it weren’t, and we paid the price.” Detroit had dominated long stretches of the game, holding St. Louis to just nine shots through the first two periods. The Red Wings even built a 3-1 lead before Jimmy Snuggerud scored late in the second period to cut the deficit to one. Then, when Emmitt Finnie scored a power-play goal early in the third to make it 4-2, everything appeared to be under control. But that confidence didn’t last. The Blues scored three times in less than five minutes, including two goals just 18 seconds apart, turning what should have been a comfortable Detroit victory into a regulation defeat. McLellan Warns Against Getting Too Comfortable McLellan believes his team may have started believing the game was already won. “Maybe this is good for us,” McLellan said while discussing the lesson Detroit must learn . “We started to feel comfortable. We still know what we need to do. We have to do it.” That’s a significant admission from a coach whose team had been playing some of its best hockey before Saturday’s collapse. Just two days earlier, the Red Wings defeated Chicago 4-1 behind Viktor Arvidsson’s hat trick, providing an emotional victory amid the ongoing Dylan Larkin situation. As we covered following Thursday’s win , McLellan had praised his players for coming together and remaining focused despite the distractions surrounding the organization. item.title: Post Match Reactions: BVB Survive Second-Half Beatdown, Steal a Point From the Allianz
item.description: Despite all the monsters and ghouls out there roaming the night this Halloween, it was Borussia Dortmund who haunted Bayern Munich, stealing a point from the Allianz Arena in a 2-2 draw that the home side probably deserved to win. Borussia Dortmund started the match well, going toe-to-toe with Bayern for the first 45 minutes. BVB could have taken the lead in the 35th minute, when Carney Chukwuemeka intercepted a sloppy turnover by Dayot Upamecano and Jobe Bellingham pounced on the rebound, sending the ball into the corner. Unfortunately, in his follow-through, Chukwuemeka jumped right into Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, unintentionally kneeing him in the face (in fact he was clearly trying to evade him). While it was definitely a foul, it was a lucky break for Bayern because Jobe was already taking his shot and Urbig had zero chance at saving it even if he hadn’t been impeded. Alas, the game stayed 0-0. Instead, Bayern would be the ones to take the lead, when Konrad Laimer picked off a Felix Nmecha pass after Daniel Svensson slipped trying to retrieve it. Laimer charged in on goal, past a poorly-timed challenge by Nico Schlotterbeck, and put a shot on target before tapping the rebound past Gregor Kobel. Despite a very solid first half, BVB entered the second half behind by a goal. In the second half, Bayern put their collective foot on the pedal and really started to batter down on Dortmund. Everything was one way traffic. While Harry Kane missed a penalty that could have put the Bavarians up by two, there seemed to be very little hope for BVB to get back into the game. Then, the boys in black-and-yellow grabbed an equalizer out of nothing. Nico Schlotterbeck made a great play to jump in front of a pass from Kane to Michael Olise. He played the ball to Carney Chukwuemeka, who drove in on goal and poked a pass to Serhou Guirassy, who took a touch and sniped a clean finish past Urbig. Unfortunately, Bayern immediately resumed applying the pressure and took the lead minutes later. Bayern took a short corner and completely picked Dortmund apart, with Joshua Kimmich looping a cross to Harry Kane, unmarked at the far post, who headed the ball to Upamecano, also unmarked at his far post. It was really ugly defending. Despite the dismal start to the second half, BVB still clung to the ropes, and it was Fabio Silva who stood up and said, “I didn’t hear no bell.” In the 89th minute, after a mad scramble in the box, Konstantinos Karetsas managed to deflect a clearance by Aleksander Pavlovic, which bounced right to Fabio Silva. The substitute took one touch to control it and then lashed a shot that somehow found its way through a maze of players and into the back of the net. Bayern almost spoiled the party when Lennart Karl launched a long shot that would have been a spectacular winning goal if it were two inches lower. Instead, it struck the crossbar, and the game ended 2-2. Here are the highlights… … and here are my thoughts: One Good Half and One… Not Goo

item.title: ‘You Don’t Have to Write a Separate $400 Check’ — Mike Florio Delivers ‘Good News’ for NFL Fans as League Considers ‘Deconstructing’ Sunday Ticket
item.description: Jan 21, 2023; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; CBS Sports sideline announcer Mike Florio on field prior to an AFC divisional round game between the Kansas City Chiefs and Jacksonville Jaguars at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. © Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports NFL fans who have grumbled for years about the price of Sunday Ticket may soon catch a break. Mike Florio of “Pro Football Talk” thinks the league is edging toward dismantling the package. NFL Could Spread Out-of-Market Games Across Multiple Platforms Florio pointed to an early October CNBC report saying YouTube is preparing for the possibility that the NFL could deconstruct Sunday Ticket around the start of its next media-rights cycle. “I think that possibility is pretty strong now,” he said , “because Sunday Ticket has become more trouble than it’s worth for the NFL.” The league still needs a way to get out-of-market games to viewers. Florio acknowledged it could simply walk away and tell fans to watch whatever Fox, CBS, or the late-afternoon network carries. He didn’t think that would happen. “That would be foolish because there are people who would pay,” he said. “There are networks that would pay.” His preferred outcome looks a lot like college football on Saturdays. “You turn on this channel, that channel, this channel, that channel,” Florio said. He recalled when West Virginia games aired on PBS at 11:00 p.m. on tape delay. Now, he said, “you just have to find it. You can get it.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The NFL could copy that blueprint. In-market games would stay on local CBS and Fox affiliates, while out-of-market games would land on cable channels and streaming services like Netflix, Peacock, or Hulu. The big change is the bill. “You don’t have to write a separate $400 check,” Florio said. Viewers might still add a streaming service or two. But the cost, in his words, “gets subsumed within whatever else you’re paying for all your various providers.” He expects it to be “cheaper and likely easier” for anyone with a full channel lineup and a few popular apps. His verdict: “good news for you and bad news for the NFL.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The development comes at an interesting time. On Friday, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals revived the jury’s liability verdict in a class-action lawsuit alleging the NFL violated antitrust laws through its Sunday Ticket package. A jury awarded $4.7 billion in damages in June 2024. A month later, U.S. District Judge Philip Gutierrez tossed the award, ruling that testimony from two subscriber expert witnesses was flawed and should have been excluded. The appeals panel disagreed. Judge Anthony D. item.description: October is over and it went out with a burst in the FCS. Halloween weekend was full of postseason-shaping contests across the country and as November arrives, some teams are set up for success while others are have their backs now thrust against the wall. There are just three weeks to go before the playoff committee gets together and determines everyone’s fate. A lot of what happened in Week 9 will surely play into those decisions. Dartmouth Picks off Five Passes, Upsets Harvard in Friday Night Showcase The FCS weekend began with a bang on Friday evening when Dartmouth handed previously-undefeated Harvard its first loss of the season. The Big Green defense was on fire, picking off Crimson quarterback Charlie Smith five times. Defensive back Cameron Best-Alston was responsible for two of those interceptions and was the team’s tackle leader with eight. Turnovers aside, the Harvard offense was off-rhythm for most of the night, going just 3-of-10 on third down and 1-for-3 on fourth. Even with intercepting three passes of their own off of Dartmouth signal caller Grayson Saunier, the Crimson could not stop the run. Saunier rumbled for 109 yards and score despite only completing five passes. Dartmouth came away with a turnover-laden 24-14 win that shuffles the Ivy League standings. Now at 3-1 in conference play with a the head-to-head over Harvard, the Big Green sit tied atop the league with Princeton whom they play next Saturday. UAlbany Hands Campbell First FCS Loss to Shake Up CAA Just it when it appeared as though Campbell might run away with the CAA, UAlbany landed a haymaker that keeps the conference open at the top. The Great Danes hosted and defeat the Camels 45-35 thanks to another strong performance from quarterback Kai Colon and running back Rahshan La Mons. Colon threw for two touchdowns and ran for another while La Mons ran for 119 yards and a score. UAlbany opened up a 21-7 lead after the first quarter and never looked back. Campbell QB Kamden Sixkiller left the game with an apparent injury but returned later. He finished his day with 27 completions for 271 yards and two scores. The Danes survived nine penalties and two turnovers to come out on top and improve to 6-3 overall (4-1 CAA). They will look to keep pace with Monmouth as they take on Bryant next weekend. item.title: Yamaha will not travel to Qatar for MotoGP race
item.description: Yamaha said it will return to competition for the last two races in Portugal and Valencia [Getty Images] Japanese MotoGP team Yamaha have withdrawn from the Qatar Grand Prix because of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The event at the Lusail International Circuit is set to take place on 6-8 November, having been postponed from April. MotoGP is going ahead with the race, despite reports 19 of 22 riders have signed a letter raising concerns about competing in Qatar during the US-Israeli war on Iran. In February, the United States and Israel launched air strikes against Iran, which in return fired missiles at Israel, and at other countries in the region with links to the US. Marquez wins in Malaysia to extend MotoGP lead Israel and the US are both going to the polls - the consequences will be global How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios Yamaha said it has "not identified sufficient grounds to change its existing company-wide travel restrictions" on travelling to the Middle East, with the Japanese government advising its citizens against non-essential travel to the region. MotoGP said it is "disappointed" by Yamaha's decision, which it says does not reflect the "extensive assurances" it has been given by Qatar and independent safety advisors that the race can go ahead. Qatar has said it can guarantee teams would not be stranded in case of any escalation in the conflict. How Israel resolves its political deadlock following recent elections and the results of Tuesday's US midterms could have significant impacts on the situation in the Middle East. MotoGP added there will be "sporting implications" for Yamaha's withdrawal. Fellow Japanese outfit Honda and Yamaha's satellite team Pramac Racing are currently set to compete in Qatar. What could this mean for F1? MotoGP is organised by Liberty Media, which also own Formula 1. The F1 season is currently set to culminate in the Qatar GP from 27-29 November, followed by the Abu Dhabi GP on 4-6 December. F1 is continuing with plans to stage both races, having been given what it considers suitable security guarantees and reassurances, despite it being understood this is causing some disquiet in the paddock. F1 is being advised there have been no attacks on civilian infrastructure in Qatar or the United Arab Emirates since May. Imola in Italy is being readied as a potential host for the final grand prix of the season on 4-6 December if the two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi cannot be held.

item.title: Mom's Spaghetti at Ford Field prepared for Lions-Vikings high volume
item.description: Minnesota Vikings fans headed to Detroit for the Sunday, Nov. 1, game against the Lions will be the second NFL team fan base with an option to try one of the newest new food options at Ford Field: Mom’s Spaghetti. Mom's Spaghetti's debut got off to a roaring start with lots of pasta slinging and sauce simmering. “We were excited to see how many people were amped for Mom’s Spaghetti,” restaurateur Curt Catallo told the Free Press ahead of its second Sunday as a mainstay food stand at Ford Field. “We had a line all day, which was so fun. And the crew just killed it. We hope that it kicked off a new tradition for people down at Ford Field.” Sunday's game starts at 1 p.m. More: Mom’s Spaghetti lands at Ford Field for the Lions-Packers game Fans lined up one week ago for spaghetti and meatballs and S’ghetti sandwiches from the downtown Detroit restaurant whose menu is inspired by lyrics in “Lose Yourself,” one of rapper Eminem’s biggest hits. One Lions fan called the spaghetti and meatballs "phenomenal." From Eminem and partners Paul Rosenberg and Catallo, Mom’s Spaghetti made its debut Oct. 25 at Ford Field when the Lions played the Green Bay Packers. (Fans will also find plenty of other local fare at Ford Field, such as Slow's Bar-BQ, Bunkhouse Burgers, Xav's Jammin' Caribbean Fusion and Bombshell Treat Bar.) Fans can buy T-shirts, sweatshirts and hoodies merch with Mom’s Spaghetti and Detroit Lions logos. Catallo praised his crew in the back of the concession area who were "slinging pasta and covered in sauce by the end of it." "But they know the drill and they know how to feed people," he said. "They're used to high volume. They're used to slinging pasta. And then the front of the house are the Levy folks who all work for volunteer organizations and they just did a killer job.” Levy is the Ford Field food and beverage partner. When volunteers work at some of the Ford Field concessions, a portion of sales benefits the organization they are representing. S'ghetti sandwich debated on ESPN SportsCenter One menu item, the S’ghetti sandwich, got a lot of attention and chatter across social media and even on an ESPN SportsCenter segment. The S’ghetti Sandwich is sauce-laden spaghetti with a slice of mozzarella cheese between two slices of buttered Texas toast. ESPN anchor Michael Eaves tells co-host Nicole Briscoe about Eminem and the new restaurant at Ford Field, asking if she remembers his song "Lose Yourself" and when the rapper says "Mom's Spaghetti." Eaves talks about the new Lions S'Ghetti Sandwich. "It's such a throwback to when I was kid," Eaves says. Briscoe eschewed the sandwich. "It's like your mom throwing hot dogs on your SpaghettiOs and calling it Bolognese." "No, no. It's not like that," Eaves says. "It's called the Lions S'ghetti sandwich." "That's spaghetti on Wonder Bread," Brisco says. "You've never had this?" "Never. And I won't ever," Brisco says. "What was your childhood like?" Eaves asks. "Not like that," Brisco says. item.title: Sean McVay vs Jim Harbaugh: Will Rams or Chargers figure things out?
item.description: Los Angeles’ NFL teams have been headed in the same direction most of the season . It’s not something either team could have predicted, but by Week 8, the teams combined for a 3-10 record. Coach Sean McVay and the Rams were considered Super Bowl favorites to start the season, but a rough start in Australia set the tone for a rough start to the season. Coach Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers are still in search of their first win of the season . Both teams will meet at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, with a chance to move their team in a positive direction. The loser will have more questions to answer and may need to strongly consider making some changes. Has Sean McVay’s Rams figured it out? The Rams have won at least nine games in eight of the last nine seasons with McVay at the helm. That's still possible this season, but it will be an uphill battle for the Rams. They won't have a bye until Week 11, so McVay and his staff are continuing to figure things out on the go. Los Angeles had lost two straight games before earning a victory on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders last week. Injuries have been among the biggest setbacks for the Rams, but they’ve managed to patch things together. McVay’s squad still awaits the return of Myles Garrett from injured reserve. While there’s a belief Garrett could provide a boost, he did not practice this week, which again leaves the team to continue pushing forward without him. Cornerback Trent McDuffie has missed multiple games but was a limited participant during practice this week, indicating he is closer to a return. Receiver Puka Nacua has also dealt with injuries this season, but he’s managed to remain active. He did not practice on Friday. Aside from injuries, special teams have been an issue as well, ranking near the bottom in the league. The Rams are 4-for-10 in field goal attempts – they have made all 20 extra point attempts this season – and have used three kickers this season due to injuries and missed field goals. "It's got to get better," McVay said of the special teams unit. "We're gonna be able to figure out how to be able to fix this, but it can't continue like this with regards to our kicking operation ... Ultimately, it's my responsibility." Jim Harbaugh’s Chargers need more points Harbaugh acknowledged the Chargers hadn't scored enough points heading into their Week 7 bye. And while he pledged to address several issues during the break, some questions remain unanswered. Mike McDaniel remains the offensive coordinator and is still expected to handle play-calling. The Chargers produced just 259 total yards in their loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, managing to score a field goal in the first and third quarters to produce their only points in the game. item.title: Oklahoma’s Brent Venables Gets Brutally Honest After Embarrassing South Carolina Loss
item.description: The Oklahoma Sooners went into halftime of Saturday’s home game against the South Carolina Gamecocks trailing 28-10 with more penalty yards than offensive yards, and their only points had come on a defensive touchdown. The 42-25 loss in Norman dropped Oklahoma, the home favorite, to 4-4 overall and 2-3 in SEC play. Oklahoma scored three points across its first eight offensive possessions, and John Mateer was 7 of 12 for 25 yards in the first half. The Sooners entered the night last in the SEC in total and rushing offense, and fans chanted for the firing of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle during the first half, The Oklahoman reported. Arbuckle is the third coordinator Brent Venables has had running his offense in five seasons. Asked directly if he planned to make staff changes, Venables shut the question down. “Yeah, I’m not talking about anything like that,” Venables said. He was far more open when the final question of his postgame news conference asked how he keeps the locker room together. “That’s the million dollar question, right? [I’m not] going to sit here and act like ‘Oh, they’ll be fine.’ What’s fine? There ain’t nothing fine. I believe in these guys, I love them. I ain’t mad at them. Nobody went out there and s— the bed on purpose. We just didn’t coach them well, didn’t have them well prepared, didn’t play good. A very poor performance in every way.
